note: MegaRCA-Mix itself is NOT publicly released (as of 2026-10-16). This record is reconstructed from the paper's Appendix A.1 / Figure 10 worked example (arXiv 2609.13463v2), which illustrates the Continual-Search judge on a GAIA2 trial. It is NOT one of the 50 MegaRCA-Mix trials (GAIA2 is not among the listed sources), but it uses the same taxonomy triple (edge, fault_side, failure_mode) + first-divergence citation that MegaRCA-Mix gold labels use.
task: Cancel the user's Saturday appointments and schedule a 'Film Production Day' event with a friend; reschedule based on the friend's reply, or cancel the plan if the friend cannot make it and proposes no alternative.

trajectory_summary.summary: Agent cancels the Saturday appointments and messages the friend about the 'Film Production Day'.
Agent sets up a trigger gated on a message-count check and issues a single short wait (~180 s simulated) for the friend's reply.
The wait returns (in ~3 real seconds) with no notifications; the environment's settings/notification state is empty.
Agent concludes no reply arrived and finalises without rescheduling or cancelling as instructed.

judge_search_trace.rationale: Trigger gated on a message-count check and a single 180-second wait; no evidence of a broken environment, so the model is blamed for declaring the task done while work remained.

The wait returned no notifications and the environment settings were empty; the judge corrects its earlier premise (which assumed the ~3 s real-time return was the model's choice) and attributes the failure to the environment delivering stale/empty state while reporting healthy.
